title: Row-level security is off on table `bookings`
detail: With RLS off, anyone holding the public anon key can read, insert, update and delete every row, including passport_number.
fix: `alter table public.bookings enable row level security;` then add one policy per action that limits rows to their owner (for example `using (auth.uid() = owner_id)`).

title: Users can change privileged column(s) role on `profiles`
detail: Policy "Users can update their own profile" allows updates and no column-level restriction exists, so a user can update their own `role` (for example make themselves an admin).
fix: `revoke update on public.profiles from authenticated, anon;` then `grant update (<safe columns>) on public.profiles to authenticated;`.

title: Policy "Admins can delete messages" depends on `is_admin()`, which trusts user-editable metadata
detail: `is_admin()` reads `user_metadata`, which any user can set for themselves with supabase.auth.updateUser, so anyone can pass this check.
fix: Make `is_admin()` read `app_metadata` or a server-controlled role column instead.

title: The service-role key is used in code that ships to the browser
detail: Anything in frontend code or in a VITE_/NEXT_PUBLIC_-style variable is bundled into the public JavaScript, so every visitor gets a key that bypasses all row-level security.
fix: Remove the service-role client from the frontend. Do admin work in an edge function that checks the caller's JWT and role, and rotate the key if it was ever deployed.

title: The service-role key is used in code that ships to the browser
detail: Anything in frontend code or in a VITE_/NEXT_PUBLIC_-style variable is bundled into the public JavaScript, so every visitor gets a key that bypasses all row-level security.
fix: Remove the service-role client from the frontend. Do admin work in an edge function that checks the caller's JWT and role, and rotate the key if it was ever deployed.

title: Edge function `export-bookings` accepts calls without a login
detail: `verify_jwt = false` lets anyone on the internet call it, and it uses the service-role key without checking who is calling, so it exposes data that row-level security would block.
fix: Remove `verify_jwt = false`, or check the caller inside the function with `supabase.auth.getUser()` before using the service-role client.

title: Policy "Profiles are viewable by everyone" lets anyone with the anon key read every row of `profiles`
detail: `using (true)` returns all rows to anyone with the anon key, including email, phone.
fix: Replace `true` with an ownership check, e.g. `using (auth.uid() = id)`, or expose only non-sensitive columns through a view.

title: Policy "Signed-in users can read messages" lets every signed-in user read every row of `messages`
detail: `using (true)` returns all rows to every signed-in user. Most apps let anyone sign up, so 'signed-in' is not a real boundary.
fix: Replace `true` with an ownership check, e.g. `using (auth.uid() = id)`, or expose only non-sensitive columns through a view.

title: Policy "Signed-in users can send messages" lets every signed-in user write any row into `messages`
detail: `with check (true)` accepts any values, so a user can create or change rows on behalf of someone else (for example setting another user's id as the sender).
fix: Check ownership in `with check`, e.g. `with check (auth.uid() = sender_id)`.

title: Security-definer function `advisor_revenue` can be called by anyone and skips row-level security
detail: Functions in the public schema are callable through the API (`/rest/v1/rpc/...`) by anon and signed-in users. This one runs as its owner, bypasses RLS and does not check who is calling.
fix: Check the caller inside the function (e.g. compare the argument with `auth.uid()`), or `revoke execute on function public.advisor_revenue from public, anon, authenticated;`.

title: Storage bucket `passports` is public
detail: Every file in a public bucket can be downloaded by anyone who has or guesses its URL; no policy applies.
fix: `update storage.buckets set public = false where id = 'passports';` and add storage policies that limit each user to their own folder.

title: Security-definer function `advisor_revenue` has no fixed search_path
detail: A security-definer function runs with its owner's rights; without `set search_path` it can be tricked into using objects from another schema.
fix: Add `set search_path = ''` and schema-qualify every table in the body.

title: Admin access is decided in the browser from user-editable metadata
detail: Hiding a page in the frontend does not protect its data, and `user_metadata` can be set by the user.
fix: Enforce admin access in the database (policies) or in an edge function, from `app_metadata`.
